description: Posts a chat agent's answer into the Teams thread it's answering, with a run-failure watcher so a crashed run is never silent, plus optional receipt-linking and reaction-based rating.

upstream_asset_key.label: Upstream Asset Key
upstream_asset_key.description: The chat agent asset to depend on and read the answer from (slash-delimited). Exactly one -- a list of more than one is a validation error.

teams_tenant_id_env_var.label: Teams Tenant Id Env Var
teams_tenant_id_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD tenant id.

teams_client_id_env_var.label: Teams Client Id Env Var
teams_client_id_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD app registration client id.

teams_client_secret_env_var.label: Teams Client Secret Env Var
teams_client_secret_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD app registration client secret.

teams_refresh_token_env_var.label: Teams Refresh Token Env Var
teams_refresh_token_env_var.description: Env var holding the INITIAL OAuth refresh token (see teams_run_request_sensor's README, 'Auth').

oauth_state_dir.label: Oauth State Dir
oauth_state_dir.description: Local path or fsspec URI dedicated to this asset's '.teams_oauth_state.json' (a rotated refresh token, if Microsoft ever issues one). Can be the SAME directory teams_agent_request_sensor uses.

answer_field.label: Answer Field
answer_field.description: Which key of the upstream asset's output dict holds the answer text. Defaults to 'final_answer' (the agent components' own documented output shape) when the upstream value is a dict; used verbatim (str()'d) otherwise.

max_chars_per_message.label: Max Chars Per Message
max_chars_per_message.description: Split or truncate (see on_long_answer) an answer longer than this many characters.

on_long_answer.label: On Long Answer
on_long_answer.description: 'split' (default): post as multiple sequential thread replies, each <= max_chars_per_message. 'truncate': post one reply, cut short with an ellipsis.

include_run_link.label: Include Run Link
include_run_link.description: Append a link to the Dagster run (requires webserver_base_url) to the last reply posted.

webserver_base_url.label: Webserver Base Url
webserver_base_url.description: Base URL of the Dagster webserver (e.g. 'http://localhost:3000' or your Dagster+ deployment URL) -- used to build the run link. Leave unset to omit the link entirely.

monitor_failures.label: Monitor Failures
monitor_failures.description: Also emit {asset_name}_failure_watcher, a run-status sensor that posts a short error reply for ANY failed run carrying teams/team_id + teams/channel_id + teams/thread_id tags -- so a crashed run is never silent in the channel. Set false to handle failure notification some other way.

error_message_template.label: Error Message Template
error_message_template.description: Template for the failure-path reply. Placeholder: {error}.

receipts_db_path.label: Receipts Db Path
receipts_db_path.description: SQLite file path -- the SAME receipts_db_path a knowledge_search_server/hybrid_knowledge_search_server the agent calls is configured with (and which must also have run_id_template set, the default, so its receipts carry this run's dagster_run_id). When set, after posting, this asset looks up every receipt this run produced and links them to the posted Teams reply/replies -- so a later rating (watch_reactions below) can find the exact receipt_id to record an outcome against. Best-effort: a lookup failure here never fails the reply post itself.

watch_reactions.label: Watch Reactions
watch_reactions.description: Also emit {asset_name}_rating_watcher, a sensor that polls reactions on every Teams reply this asset has linked to a receipt (via receipts_db_path, which must also be set) and records a thumbs_up/thumbs_down outcome against each linked receipt_id -- the reactor's resolved email (see resolve_rater_email) becomes the outcome's `outcome_ref`, so changing a reaction later supersedes the earlier rating instead of double-counting. Needs delegated ChannelMessage.Send (the same scope already provisioned for posting) -- confirmed against Microsoft's own Graph reference, reading a message's own `reactions[]` needs no separate scope at all.

positive_reaction.label: Positive Reaction
positive_reaction.description: Reaction (any Unicode emoji character, or a legacy name like 'like') that records a thumbs_up outcome. Only used when watch_reactions is true.

negative_reaction.label: Negative Reaction
negative_reaction.description: Reaction that records a thumbs_down outcome. Only used when watch_reactions is true.

rating_poll_interval_seconds.label: Rating Poll Interval Seconds
rating_poll_interval_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between rating_watcher ticks. Only used when watch_reactions is true.

rating_lookback_messages.label: Rating Lookback Messages
rating_lookback_messages.description: Most-recently-linked replies to keep polling for reactions, and the cursor's bound. Only used when watch_reactions is true.

resolve_rater_email.label: Resolve Rater Email
resolve_rater_email.description: Resolve the reacting user's Azure AD object id to an email address (needs delegated User.Read.All) before using it as the outcome's outcome_ref. When false, the raw Azure AD object id is used instead. Only used when watch_reactions is true.

deps.label: Deps
deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys, beyond upstream_asset_key -- no value loaded.

owners.label: Owners
owners.description: Asset owners -- team names ('team:analytics') or email addresses.

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags
